findings.summary: The correction added to M5.27 replaces one false reason with another: part (2) went stale because M5.2 made it TRUE, not because a line number moved
findings.detail: The staged M5.27 cell now reads "`e19038e` hoisted the REQUEST into a named local; the `flushSeq++` is still inside that constructor call today. What made part (2) stale was the line number, not the increment moving". The first two clauses are true and I verified them (`git show e19038e` is a pure introduce-explaining-variable; the increment is at DefaultIngest.java:389 inside `new CommitRequest(...)`). The last clause is false. Part (2) at M5's start (66f4020, SPEC.md line 199) read: "the retry reuses the same triple -- **false today**: `DefaultIngest.java:355` writes `flushSeq++` at the call site, and `Sequencer`'s contract says 'THIS GUARANTEE STOPS AT THIS SEAM...'". What M5.27 actually changed (d043479, SPEC.md:221) was the VERDICT: "the retry reuses the same triple -- **true since M5.2**, which builds the `CommitRequest` once so a resend carries the triple the first attempt used". So part (2) went stale because the hoist falsified its verdict, and secondarily because the `Sequencer` clause it quoted was replaced by M5.23 -- the line number is the least of three causes, and the staged sentence names it as the only one. Failure scenario: a reader auditing M5's prerequisites reads this row and concludes M5.2 changed nothing part (2) asserted -- i.e. that a retry still mints a different triple and only a line reference drifted -- which contradicts SPEC.md:221, SPEC.md:99-100 and this same file's M5.2 row at backlog.md:70, and would have them re-open a prerequisite that is built. This is the defect class M5.32 exists to remove, introduced by M5.32.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader auditing M5's prerequisites reads this row, concludes M5.2 changed nothing part (2) asserted -- that a retry still mints a different triple and only a line reference drifted -- and re-opens or re-does a prerequisite that is already built, while the tree now asserts both answers (SPEC.md:221 'true since M5.2' against this cell).

findings.summary: Flipping M5.32 to done leaves SPEC.md's acceptance criterion 4 and its Scope item 3 naming M5.32 as the owner of a property that is still unpinned, and no row owns the production resend
findings.detail: SPEC.md:101-104 says "NOTHING PINS IT: review MEASURED that reverting M5.2 leaves the whole suite green ... Recorded as M5.32", and SPEC.md:320-324 (acceptance criterion 4, "A retry reuses its triple end to end") says "STILL UNMET, and not for the reason first written: M5.2 makes the request resendable, but no production caller resends an ambiguous commit ... M5.32." Both pointers become dangling the moment this row reads done: M5.32's own State cell concludes the pin cannot exist until a PRODUCTION resend exists, and no backlog row owns writing one -- M5.6e owns the transport only (todo, owned by M8), M5.23 explicitly says "the resend is now SAFE AGAINST THE SAME SEQUENCER, nothing yet MAKES one", and M5.20 owns only the multi-pod-hole sweep and VERIFIED.md. Failure scenario: M5.20 walks the acceptance criteria for VERIFIED.md, reads criterion 4's "STILL UNMET ... M5.32", opens the backlog, finds M5.32 **done**, and records criterion 4 as met -- a false milestone completion claim with nothing downstream able to catch it. The commit already edits SPEC.md, so re-pointing those two sites (or adding the row that owns the end-to-end pin) is one sentence, and this file's own convention is to re-home rather than close (see M5.25's "TWO ITEMS THIS ROW ONCE OWNED ARE NOT CLOSED HERE and are re-homed").
findings.failure_scenario: M5.20 walks the acceptance criteria for M5's VERIFIED.md, reads criterion 4's 'STILL UNMET ... M5.32', opens the backlog, finds M5.32 marked done, and records criterion 4 as met -- a false milestone completion claim, with the production resend that would actually meet it owned by no row at all.

findings.summary: "`SPEC.md` §3 had it right all along" is false: §3's correct wording is two commits old, written by M5.27, which then missed its own Tasks row
findings.detail: Measured: from M5.0 (66f4020) to M5.27 (d043479), SPEC.md §3 read "`DefaultIngest.java:355` writes `flushSeq++` at the commit call site, so a retry mints a DIFFERENT triple and the leaseholder's dedup cannot match it" -- word for word the sentence the backlog M5.2 row carries, i.e. the two AGREED. The sentence the cell credits ("hoists the request into a named local ...; the `flushSeq++` itself still sits in that constructor call, and moving it was never the point") was introduced by d043479. So the SPEC did not contradict itself "all along"; it began contradicting itself at M5.27, which corrected §3 and left the Tasks row 320 lines below untouched while its own cell claims a five-site sweep of that file. The same claim is restated at backlog.md:70 ("`SPEC.md` §3 has said so all along while this row said the opposite"). Failure scenario: a reader treats §3 as a source that predates the confusion and therefore needs no audit, and misses the real lesson -- that M5.27's in-file sweep was incomplete, which is what would justify a mechanism rather than a fourth manual sweep.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader treats SPEC.md §3 as a source that predates the confusion and so needs no audit, missing that §3's correctness is two commits old and that M5.27's in-file sweep corrected §3 while leaving its own Tasks row 320 lines below -- the fact that would justify a mechanism instead of a fourth manual sweep.

findings.summary: M5.34's handoff paragraph is appended to the Serves column, not the Task column
findings.detail: The table header is `| ID | Task | Serves | State |`. The staged row reads `... outcome-identical | FR-11 ⚠️ **AND M5.32 HANDS THIS ROW A FOURTH SITE**, ... the increment was not | todo |`, putting ~600 characters of narrative in the requirement-ID cell; M5.27's analogous handoff went into the Task cell. This is the only row in the file whose Serves cell is not a bare ID or `—` (29 rows read `| FR-11 |`). sdd.md rule 2 makes that column the requirement citation. It is worse when rendered: that row already carries unescaped pipes from the code span `` `!hasPointer() || incarnationId() == null` `` (pre-existing), so the row has six cells against a four-column header and GFM drops the excess -- the handoff text and `todo` are both in the dropped region. Failure scenario: whoever picks up M5.34 from a rendered backlog never sees the fourth site handed to it, and the deferred `DefaultIngest.java:384` correction is lost.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M5.34 from a rendered backlog never sees the fourth site handed to it -- the row already has six cells against a four-column header, so the appended text and the State cell are both dropped -- and the deferred DefaultIngest.java:384 correction is lost with M5.32 already closed.

findings.summary: A fifth site carries the same implication, uncounted by "FOUR SITES, NOT ONE" and handed to nobody
findings.detail: The class javadoc of the class named for the property reads "{@code DefaultIngest} wrote {@code flushSeq++} inside the {@code CommitRequest} constructor call, so the request could not be resent at all. It is now a named local, which is the whole change." Past tense plus "now" implies the increment left that constructor call; it did not (DefaultIngest.java:389). This is the same family as the deferred src/main comment, it is in the file a reader opens to learn what the property means, and the staged cell's enumeration is an explicit count -- "FOUR SITES, NOT ONE" -- which is falsified by it. Failure scenario: M5.34 works the handed-over list, fixes DefaultIngest.java:384, and this site survives, so the next sweep finds the claim still standing -- exactly how M5.34's own row records the limit count going wrong three times.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.34 works the handed-over list, fixes DefaultIngest.java:384, and this fifth site survives uncounted, so the next sweep finds the same claim still standing in the class named for the property -- the same way M5.34's own row records the limit count going wrong three times.

findings.summary: The M5.2 row's retained present-tense sentence is now false of the tree, in the cell this commit rewrote
findings.detail: After the new correction the row still reads "⚠️ `DefaultIngest.java:355` writes `flushSeq++` at the commit call site, so a retry mints a DIFFERENT triple and the leaseholder's dedup cannot match it", in the present tense and unmarked. Line 355 is no longer that code (it is 389), and the consequence clause is what M5.2 falsified -- SPEC.md:221 says the retry now reuses the triple. Keeping the original sentence as history is this file's convention, but it needs the same "true AT M5'S START" marking M5.27's cell says it applied to the five SPEC sites. Failure scenario: a reader skims past the new preamble to the ⚠️ sentence -- the format that usually carries the current caveat in this file -- and takes the falsified claim as today's state; it is also the sentence that makes the M5.27 'line number' correction above look right.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader skims past the new preamble to the ⚠️ sentence -- the format that carries the CURRENT caveat everywhere else in this file -- and takes 'DefaultIngest.java:355 writes flushSeq++ at the commit call site, so a retry mints a DIFFERENT triple' as today's state, when both the line number and the consequence are false.
